units.title: Third day of fog: the Sound waits for a wind
units.author: courier
units.text: The Marrow Sound woke to a third morning of fog, and forecasters say a front that could clear it is still three or four days away. Carrow Point recorded visibility of 40 metres overnight, and the headland's automated fog signal sounded for fourteen hours without a break.

units.author: courier
units.text: Shops in Gilliver report brisk sales of torches, batteries and draught excluders. The chandlery on Harbour Road said it had sold out of reflective armbands by Thursday lunchtime. The owner said most were bought by parents for children walking to the school bus along the unlit section of the front.

units.author: courier
units.text: The ferry has kept running throughout, though rarely on time. Commuters from Lisle say the morning crossing now takes nearly twice as long. A regular passenger said the crew had been patient and good-humoured, and the only real complaint was that the cafe ran out of bacon rolls before Lisle.

units.author: courier
units.text: Local weather watchers have been enjoying it more than most. A retired surveyor who runs a weather station near Carrow Point described the conditions as textbook advection fog and said he had recorded the dew point and air temperature within half a degree of each other for sixty hours.

units.title: Harbour office reminds public to keep off slipways after ferry report
units.author: soundfm
units.text: Gilliver harbour office has reminded the public to stay off the slipway after dark, after the crew of a night ferry reported seeing someone standing at the end of the slip in thick fog earlier this week. The person did not respond when hailed, and the ferry held off until the crew could no longer see them.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: The harbourmaster said the report had been logged as a trespass and that there was no suggestion anyone had come to harm. She said people sometimes walk to the end of the slip to fish or to watch the boat come in, but in fog the crew cannot judge distance and a person near the water's edge is at real risk.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: Sound Lines confirmed the report and thanked its crew for following procedure. Four street lights near the slip are currently out because of a cable fault, which the company said did not help. The council says a contractor will repair them as soon as possible.

units.title: Live: fog, day three
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 06:40 ST. Power is off in parts of Lisle west after a cable fault just before six. Sound Power says engineers are on the first boat. The fog is as thick as yesterday, and the first Port Ammet sailing is about half an hour late.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 07:35 ST. Lisle primary is open but running on emergency lighting until the power returns. The head says the children are treating it as an adventure. A listener on the reservoir road reports black ice beside the dam gates, so please take it slowly.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 09:25 ST. Most of Lisle west is back on. Eleven properties still waiting while engineers finish a temporary link. The Met Office has extended the fog advisory until further notice, so this page is going to be with you for a while.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 12:30 ST. A brief bright patch over Port Ammet. Somebody on the harbour wall has been photographing the edge of the fog bank sitting just offshore like a wall. Lisle and Gilliver remain completely grey.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 15:10 ST. Sound Lines says freight and charter runs are being shuffled around the passenger timetable. Operators with regular supply runs will hear directly from the freight desk. Passenger sailings keep their slots but expect delays.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 18:05 ST. Visibility at the Brackwater reservoir is down to about 30 metres in freezing fog. The gritters are already out. Carrow Point residents ask us to say, politely, that they would like the fog signal to stop. The coastguard says politely that it won't.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 19:50 ST. Night ferry expected up to 45 minutes late. Gilliver passengers please use the harbour shelter. That is all from the day desk. Thank you for sending in your fog photos; we have now received forty-one pictures of a lamp post.

units.title: Tower block tenants call meeting over dark stairwell
units.author: weypost
units.text: The residents' association at Dellow Court has called an open meeting for next week after a run of complaints about stairwell lights cutting out between the sixth and eighth floors. With the lift still broken, most residents have no other way in or out of the building.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The association's secretary said she had collected more than a dozen reports in a week, some from elderly residents who now wait for a neighbour before using the stairs at night. She described the problem as a maintenance issue, which she said was still an issue, and asked the managing agent to attend.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Some residents have described hearing footsteps on the stairs when the lights go out, which the Post understands has been discussed at length on the residents' online message board. One resident said the stairwell had always been noisy and that sound travels oddly in concrete.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Kerrow Estates said it was aware of reports regarding the stairwell lighting and that a contractor would be asked to inspect the circuit. It said there was no evidence of unauthorised access to the building. The replacement lift part is expected next week.

units.title: Living on the job: the return of the island camp
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: The live-in work camp, once a fixture of northern forestry, is having a small revival on coastal jobs where daily crew transport costs more than accommodation. The Kittering Holm contract is the most visible current example, with a crew living on site for the whole of a thirty-day clearance.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Veterans of older camps say the practical problems have not changed: drying clothes, keeping a generator fed, and keeping a small group cheerful in the dark months. One retired site lead said the most important piece of kit on any camp he ran was a good kettle, and the second was a clear rule about who stays awake.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Modern camps are usually a converted camper or cabin with bunks, a stove and a satellite link. Welfare guidance recommends a fixed rest period, a daily check-in with the office and a written plan for getting people off site in bad weather. Inspectors say the plans are often written and rarely tested.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Grieve Land Services said in a brief statement that its Holm camp met all current welfare standards and that its crew were in regular contact with head office. The firm declined to discuss progress on the contract, citing client confidentiality.

units.title: Holm plans: council says the paperwork is public
units.author: courier
units.text: Ammet District Council has reminded residents that planning documents for the Kittering Holm clearance are open to inspection, after a week in which theories about the island's future have spread on local message boards. Suggestions have ranged from a luxury retreat to a data centre.

units.author: courier
units.text: A council spokesperson said the approved application covers vegetation clearance only and does not include any building. Any future construction would need a separate application, which would be advertised in the usual way and open to public comment.

units.author: courier
units.text: Ardent Vale Holdings repeated that it had no plans to announce. A planning consultant who follows local applications told the Courier there was nothing unusual about clearing land before deciding what to do with it, though she said the scale and speed of this job were unusual for the Sound.

units.author: courier
units.text: In Gilliver, where the island fills the view from the harbour, people were more interested in the boats than the theories. A fuel berth attendant said he had sold more diesel this week than in the whole of September, and that whatever they were building, he hoped it would need diesel too.

units.title: Canal Street night market called off for fog
units.author: weypost
units.text: Organisers of the Canal Street night market have postponed tomorrow's event after a second week of poor visibility along the canal. Stallholders said they had lost money last week when the fog kept shoppers away and food went unsold. The market will return on the first clear Friday.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The towpath lighting along the market stretch is also partly out, which organisers said made the decision easier. The city council said the lights are on a list for repair and that it is aware of complaints from residents of the canal-side blocks.

units.author: weypost
units.text: A stallholder who sells soup from a converted van said she would trade from her usual pitch anyway, fog or not, because her regulars were night workers who came whatever the weather. She said she would light the van with every lamp she owned so they could find her.

units.title: Lisle lifeboat open day postponed
units.author: courier
units.text: The Lisle lifeboat station has postponed its autumn open day, which had been due this weekend, because visiting boats and the planned demonstration launch cannot run safely in fog. Volunteers said the raffle prizes, including a hamper donated by the Lisle bakery, would be kept for the new date.

units.author: courier
units.text: The crew has not been idle. It launched twice this week to help small craft unable to find their way, both times in visibility under 100 metres. The coxswain said both calls ended well because the people involved had radios and called early instead of trying to find their own way home.

units.author: courier
units.text: The station is still looking for shore crew volunteers, particularly people who live within five minutes of the boathouse. No sailing experience is needed. Training is on Tuesday evenings, with tea and, the coxswain promised, better biscuits than last year.

units.title: Softwood prices ease as autumn supply rises
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Merchants in the northern districts report a modest fall in softwood log prices this month as autumn felling picks up and mills work through stock. Firewood prices have moved the other way, rising for the third month as households prepare for winter.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Several merchants noted that large clearance jobs can unsettle local prices if a lot of timber arrives at once. One Weyhaven yard said it had been asked informally whether it could take Holm timber and had said yes, but no contract had followed. The yard assumes the wood will be chipped or left on site.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Chainsaw dealers report strong sales of replacement chains and bars, with one Tollinby supplier describing the first week of the month as 'Christmas come early'. Fuel costs for saws and generators remain the largest single running expense for small contractors.

units.title: Carrow Point neighbours ask for quieter fog signal
units.author: soundfm
units.text: Residents of the cottages nearest Carrow Point lighthouse say they have barely slept since the automated fog signal began sounding on Tuesday evening. The signal blasts every thirty seconds whenever visibility at the station drops below two nautical miles, which this week has been nearly all the time.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: The coastguard said the signal is a statutory aid to navigation and cannot be turned down. A spokesperson added that in still fog the sound can be hard for vessels to place, which is exactly when it matters. Residents were offered information about ear plugs, which one described as unhelpful.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: One neighbour who has lived on the headland for thirty years said she remembered the days when keepers ran the light and you could knock on the door to complain. She said she would not swap, though, because when the fog signal stops in the night you notice how quiet the shore road is.
